answer:
Run the eval with the `-j 1` option:

```bash
promptfoo eval -j 1
```

The docs say that "you can run evals serially using the `-j 1` option" [promptfoo/site/docs/providers/ollama.md]. They also say that "This serializes the eval's **target** calls: one provider and prompt at a time." [promptfoo/site/docs/providers/ollama.md]

Two caveats from the same section:

- **Test-case order isn't strict.** "the evaluator runs test cases marked `options.runSerially` as a separate partition ahead of the rest, so a config using that option does not execute in strict test-case order even at `-j 1`." [promptfoo/site/docs/providers/ollama.md]
- **Model-graded assertions can still overlap.** Grader calls are serialized only when grouping is active. If grouping is disabled, "up to `PROMPTFOO_ASSERTIONS_MAX_CONCURRENCY` grader calls (3 by default) can still overlap within a single test case." This happens with a per-eval timeout or a `{{_conversation}}` variable. [promptfoo/site/docs/providers/ollama.md]
